_comment: Expert-authored config, not derived from any corpus or pack - see .claude/classic-beats-full-kit.md and the cited sources there (Wikipedia's One-drop rhythm, bassculture.substack.com, MusicRadar's one-drop-fill tutorial, Modern Drummer's steppers article). Each style's 'variations' are the genuinely different arrangement choice a real drummer plays for a second take (articulation swap, an added accent) - not timing/velocity noise.

styles.expert_notes: Carlton Barrett's one-drop: beat 1 is left empty (no kick at all), and the kick lands together with the snare accent on beat 3 - the 'drop'. The snare accent is a cross-stick/rimshot click, not a full snare hit; that dry, woody sound is the style's defining signature. Hihat plays steady 8ths throughout.

variations.name: chorus
variations.expert_notes: A documented busier-chorus move: an extra cross-stick on the 'and' of beat 4, layered on top of the same rimshot-on-3 foundation.

styles.expert_notes: Rockers puts the emphasis back on the downbeat: it adds a kick on beat 1 to the one-drop's own beat-3 kick+rimshot, filling in what one-drop leaves empty, for a more forward-driving feel. Sources disagree on whether rockers' backbeat sits on beat 3 alone or on 2-and-4; this config follows the throughline version connecting all three styles (kick on 1 and 3, accent on 3) since it reads as a clear intensification of one-drop rather than an unrelated pattern.

variations.name: chorus
variations.expert_notes: Swapping the verse's rimshot for a full snare hit - the same rimshot-vs-full-snare device one-drop's chorus variation uses differently - is a common, simple way to raise the energy into a chorus.

styles.expert_notes: Steppers takes rockers' kick density further: a steady four-on-the-floor kick on every beat (a driving, 'marching' quality), while the beat-3 rimshot accent and steady hihat carry over from one-drop/rockers.

variations.name: chorus
variations.expert_notes: Opening the hihat on an 'and' between beats for a dubbier chorus texture, a commonly cited reggae hihat device.
